report_name: BigCommerce Data Breach Caused by Compromised Third-Party App

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Software Supply Chain
attack_patterns.description: Attackers compromised the third-party 'Ribon' application to gain access to the BigCommerce platform, representing a software supply chain attack.

attack_patterns.name: Steal Application Access Token
attack_patterns.description: Attackers stole a BigCommerce application key belonging to the Ribon app to gain unauthorized API access.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Cloud Storage
attack_patterns.description: Attackers used unauthorized API access to exfiltrate customer PII (names, emails, phone numbers, shipping addresses) from BigCommerce stores.

tools.name: Ribon
tools.description: A third-party application for BigCommerce storefronts whose application key was compromised and used by attackers to access merchant data.

campaigns.name: BigCommerce Ribon App Supply-Chain Attack
campaigns.description: A supply-chain attack where a compromised application key for the 'Ribon' app was used to access and exfiltrate customer data from BigCommerce merchants between September 13 and 17, 2026.

identities.name: BigCommerce
identities.description: The e-commerce platform whose merchants were affected by a supply-chain attack originating from the compromised Ribon app.

identities.name: Master of Malt
identities.description: A BigCommerce merchant and victim of the data breach who notified customers and the UK ICO.

identities.name: Be A Part Of
identities.description: The developer of the compromised 'Ribon' and 'Ribon 1.5' applications.

identities.name: Information Commissioner's Office (ICO)
identities.description: The UK's data protection authority that was notified of the breach by Master of Malt.

infrastructure.name: BigCommerce API
infrastructure.description: The API of the BigCommerce platform that was accessed by attackers using a stolen third-party application key to exfiltrate customer data.

indicators.name: Excessive API GET Requests for Customer PII
indicators.pattern:
title: Excessive API GET Requests for Customer PII
id: 1a2b3c4d-5e6f-4a9b-8c7d-6e5f4a3b2c1d
status: experimental
description: Detects GET requests to common customer or order API endpoints. A high volume of these requests from a single source may indicate data exfiltration, as seen in the BigCommerce supply-chain attack. This rule is intended for threat hunting and requires correlation on source IP or API key.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-22
tags:
  - attack.t1530
level: low
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection:
    cs-method: 'GET'
    cs-uri-stem|contains:
      - '/api/v3/customers'
      - '/api/v2/orders'
      - '/customers'
      - '/orders'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects an excessive number of GET requests to API endpoints that return customer PII (e.g., /customers, /orders), especially if originating from a single API key over a short period. This may indicate a supply-chain attack.

relationships.source_name: Excessive API GET Requests for Customer PII
